q: Why rebuild the triage queue before drawing a conclusion in the lab?
options: It reproduces alerts from the defined exercise dataset
It automatically confirms the cause of each highlighted event
It establishes that every asset in the organization was monitored
It replaces the need to document how the incident was noticed
explanation: Rebuilding the queue gives an auditable starting point for triage.

q: The hunt reports no other hosts with the same observed pattern. What can the analyst conclude?
options: No other host can have been affected anywhere on the corporate network
The search found no matching hosts in the selected telemetry and time window
All events from the affected subnet were ingested with complete coverage
The suspected case qualifies for closure without collecting endpoint evidence
explanation: Negative results are bounded by the query and available visibility.

q: A case report labels the upload as confirmed exposure of payroll records. Which rewrite is defensible?
options: Payroll records were disclosed because the upload destination was unfamiliar
No sensitive information could have left because contents were not logged
A transfer of 48.2 MB was observed, while its contents remain unknown
The recorded upload shows which file types the remote receiver retained
explanation: Transfer metadata does not establish the payload's contents.

q: What is the purpose of labeling timeline entries observed or inferred?
options: It grants inferred entries a higher evidentiary status than source records
It lets reviewers skip any event that has not been assigned a verdict
It replaces the need for timestamps and source labels in the incident report
It lets reviewers distinguish recorded events from analyst conclusions
explanation: Labels preserve the difference between what a record shows and what it suggests.

q: An analyst wants to merge the endpoint and VPN threads into one confirmed causal chain. What should the lead require?
options: Evidence linking the two threads, with the current relationship logged as a hypothesis
Agreement from both queue owners that a single case would be simpler to manage
A sufficiently close time window even if there is no shared supporting evidence
A matching alert severity on both threads before marking the account compromised
explanation: Temporal overlap supports investigation, while a confirmed link needs corroboration.

q: Why coordinate endpoint isolation with the identity response?
options: It allows all teams to skip recording the effective time of each action
It reduces the time that an identified access path remains open
It keeps the queue from receiving new alarms after the exercise closes
It makes later verification unnecessary because all teams acted together
explanation: Coordination closes related paths promptly and each control still needs verification.

q: Who should receive the noticed time and factual summary for the reporting decision?
options: All employees and contractors through a company-wide emergency broadcast
The owner of the original source alert regardless of incident role
The designated legal or reporting owner through the case workflow
The student who entered the timestamp into the mock incident register
explanation: The SOC provides a factual handoff to the responsible reporting role.

q: What does recomputing a mismatched digest on a working copy establish?
options: The analyst who changed the file can be identified from the digest alone
The exported source record was fabricated before the first collection
The revised file is acceptable because its new digest is internally consistent
The current bytes differ from the bytes represented by the saved digest
explanation: A hash mismatch signals changed bytes but does not explain who changed them or why.

q: Why check an evidence package after adding the analyst's timeline file?
options: So the manifest covers the finalized files being delivered
So the new timeline can replace the original evidence everywhere
So the incident ticket can be closed without a custody entry
So a matching digest can identify which timeline observations were inferred
explanation: Files added after an initial export need to be covered by final package verification.

q: The analyst changes a test copy to demonstrate tamper detection. What should happen to the original package?
options: Replace the original with the test copy after recording the expected error
Keep the original intact and verify it independently
Update the original manifest to contain the intentionally modified copy's digest
Remove the original after collecting a screenshot of the failed verification
explanation: A tamper test belongs on a copy, with the deliverable preserved.

q: What makes a merged timeline reproducible across reviewers?
options: A screenshot of the latest triage dashboard alone
A remote analyst recollection of the observed ordering
A documented query, dataset and time range
A single summary sentence in the closure note
explanation: The input and query let another reviewer regenerate the underlying rows.

q: How should the incident report handle uncertain attribution to a specific person?
options: Treat account ownership as conclusive evidence of who performed each action
Use the employee's name in the executive summary before identity logs are reviewed
Discard all records associated with the account until attribution is resolved
Describe the observed account activity and record any actor attribution as unresolved
explanation: Records identify an account or session more readily than the person behind it.

q: An endpoint can be isolated from the network through the approved management tool. Why does the exercise prefer this to powering it off?
options: It limits network access while preserving live memory for authorized collection
It guarantees that all in-memory evidence has already been sent to the SIEM
It removes the need to identify the incident lead and the executing team
It cancels any requirement to maintain custody documentation for the endpoint
explanation: Isolation can reduce harm without the same immediate loss of volatile state.

q: Which note belongs next to each containment recommendation?
options: The surname of the student who ran the training lab last
The executing owner, dependency, and evidence impact
The next scheduled feature release for the course website
The longest description of an unrelated control being evaluated
explanation: Containment advice should be actionable and make tradeoffs visible.

q: A block rule begins matching traffic from a different machine. What should the SOC do with that observation?
options: Treat it as proof that the existing endpoint isolation failed completely
Remove the rule and delete the alert to avoid duplicate incident records
Preserve it and investigate the machine as a potential additional lead
Close the case because the block rule is absorbing all remaining risk
explanation: A new match may widen the investigation and needs independent context.

q: The incident ticket is ready for a shift change. What supports effective handoff?
options: A chronological copy of chat messages without decisions or owners
Only the names of reports created by everyone on the previous shift
The archived raw export without a case summary or follow-up steps
Current scope, open hypotheses, deadlines, and next actions
explanation: A handoff makes unresolved work, ownership, and timing clear.

q: The analyst notices the case record uses the tabletop's 08:30 UTC. Which lab deadline should be entered?
options: 14:30 UTC and 20:00 IST, based on exercise notice
14:25 UTC and 19:55 IST, based on the review exercise
14:50 UTC and 20:20 IST, based on the legal handoff
15:05 UTC and 20:35 IST, based on the isolate decision
explanation: This exercise measures from its own notice record rather than an earlier example.

q: What does a successful manifest check allow the analyst to report?
options: The initial export contains every relevant event from the incident
The delivered files match the recorded digests
The timeline's inferences are independently proven by the export
The evidence has no privacy restrictions after transfer to another team
explanation: Hash verification confirms file integrity relative to the manifest.

q: A negative VPN check excludes the relevant subnet. What is the best correction?
options: Broaden the incident to every monitored account because the first check was flawed
Leave the original result intact and describe it as a complete search
Rerun it with the intended scope and amend the bounded finding
Merge it with a positive proxy result and treat the combined output as exhaustive
explanation: The intended coverage needs a corresponding query and clearly revised record.

q: What is the proper environment for the incident-handling lab?
options: A corporate SOC queue that contains live investigatory records
A personal mailbox with actual suspicious messages awaiting review
The production system used by the exercise's vendor partner
An isolated exercise environment with the provided dataset
explanation: The course lab uses its controlled dataset rather than real systems.

q: A reviewer wants to see how a finding moved from a raw event to the final report. What should the analyst provide?
options: The source reference, timeline row, and supporting reasoning for the finding
The final conclusion and a screenshot of the completed quiz results
The root-cause label and a revised chart without any record identifiers
An unsigned copy of a different incident that used the same terminology
explanation: Traceability lets reviewers follow evidence through interpretation to the conclusion.

q: Before declaring a contained path closed, what should the analyst check?
options: Whether the ticket assigned to the team was marked as started
Evidence that the control took effect in the intended scope
Whether the mitigation appears in every version of the training notes
Whether the case title accurately shows the current course module name
explanation: Closure requires evidence of effective containment within the target scope.

q: Identity logs show a successful VPN session after a series of failures. What is the appropriate report entry?
options: Confirm the user committed the endpoint activity because the login is close in time
Treat the successful authentication as proof that no compromise occurred
Record the successful session and investigate whether the related account was compromised
Exclude the authentication record until it can be mapped to a workstation process
explanation: The success is observed, while account compromise and linkage need evidence.

q: Which exercise output documents facts, confidence, and proposed response in one place?
options: The original event dataset
The hash manifest alone
The lab setup checklist
The incident report
explanation: The incident report synthesizes evidence, gaps, and next actions for decision makers.

q: The case owner asks whether scoping should wait for a full forensic image before notifying legal. How should the SOC respond?
options: Send the timed factual handoff now and update it as evidence improves
Wait until every possibility is resolved before giving legal the noticed time
Send only the forensic image once available because it contains the complete case record
Start the reporting clock when the image is complete to give legal verified facts
explanation: The reporting handoff can proceed in parallel with scoping and collection.
